title: Config-triggered eval gating and permissioned prompt library lifecycle
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Problem: Config and model changes (e.g., kernel selection, quantization profile, sequence length defaults) are being deployed without a consistent, automated eval gate. When a model/config change regresses quality on critical prompt collections (golden datasets), detection is slow and rollbacks are manual. This ticket defines a product workflow to tie config/model changes to curated prompt libraries, gated evals, and permissioned stewardship so changes can be blocked automatically or surfaced for human review.
acceptance_criteria:
[1] For any model or serving-config change submitted to the rollout pipeline, the platform runs a configurable eval suite against the linked golden prompt set within the same commit window.
[2] If key metrics (ROUGE-like, pass@k, hallucination rate, safety signals) exceed configurable thresholds, the rollout is automatically paused and an incident ticket is created.
[3] Prompt libraries are version-controlled and immutable after signing; owners can create new versions with a recorded diff, signer, and rationale.
[4] Fine-grained ACLs allow teams to restrict who can enroll prompts into a production gate and who can approve gate overrides.
[5] Console shows per-release gating status, failing prompts, and the delta metrics with links to the failing examples.
[6] Migration path documented for existing golden sets and a rollback playbook for emergency unblocks.
tasks: Define schema for linking a rollout (model/config change) to a prompt library version
Implement a signer + immutable snapshot flow for golden promptsets
Add ACL model to prompt library metadata and UI affordances
Build an eval-runner hook in the rollout orchestration that executes the linked promptset
Define default metric thresholds and allow per-project overrides
Console: gating dashboard and alerting integration (PagerDuty/Slack)
Document migration & rollback playbook and run tabletop exercise
notes: Initial spike completed by ENG spike team (notes in Drive: https://drive.redwood/example-spike-eval-hooks).
Trade-offs discussed: automatic blocking reduces human review burden but increases risk of false-positives. Plan is to ship with conservative defaults and an override path with audit logging.
We will reuse existing eval infra (ENG-9849 style runners) but add job provenance so a failed gate points to the exact config commit and model variant.
Security: golden promptsets may contain customer-like examples. Marking this for security review to ensure storage/encryption/KMS usage aligns with Private deployments.
review_feedback: Design review (Maya Chen): ask for compact diff view of prompt changes and a change rationale field
Engineering (Marco Silva): prefer running evals in isolated short-lived pods to avoid noisy multi-tenant interference
Security (Aisha Khan): require encryption-at-rest and KMS key-scoped access for production goldens
decision_log: Choose immutable signed snapshots vs mutable live libraries: decided signed snapshots to enable reproducible evals and cryptographic audit trails
Gating behavior default: conservative block + human-in-the-loop override with 24-hour auto-escalation
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): MVP backend: link schema + eval-runner hook + minimal console view in staging. Phase 2 (3 weeks): ACLs, signer UI, and alerts. Phase 3 (2 weeks): migration tools for existing sets + tabletop exercise + GA on hosted and Dedicated. Disable auto-block for first 2 internal releases to collect telemetry.
migration_steps: 1) Inventory existing golden promptsets and owners (script: gs://redwood-goldens/inventory-csv). 2) Run automatic snapshot converter to produce signed versions and surface diffs for owner approval. 3) Owners verify and approve converted versions. 4) Update rollout pipelines to reference new snapshot ids.
metrics_and_sla: Primary metric: % of rollouts paused by gate that were true positives (target > 80% after tuning). Secondary: mean time to unblock for false-positives (target < 6 hours with on-call support). Monitor false-positive rate and eval runtime distribution.
customer_notes: Enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private will be able to opt for stricter default thresholds; expose a tenant-level toggle in Admin Console. Communicate changes to customers with managed Dedicated contracts two weeks before GA.
open_questions: What is the canonical set of automated evaluation metrics for each workload type? (chat vs classification vs code)
Should we allow composite gates (OR/AND across metrics) at the project level?
How do we handle private promptsets that cannot leave a customer's VPC during eval runs?
